classes.name: ErrorMgrThread
classes.docu:
ErrorMgrThread runs a Runnable and catches any Errors that throw from
the Runnable.run(). Like any other Thread, an ErrorMgrThread will inherit
the ErrorMgr configuration of its parent Thread. Specifically, if the
parent Thread has an ErrorHandler, the ErrorMgrThread will inherit that
ErrorHandler and it will be that ErrorHandler which will be in effect
unless ErrorMgr.setErrorHandler() is called within Runnable.run().

If an Error is thrown out of Runnable.run() then then ErrorMgrThread.run()
checks to see if an ErrorHandler is installed on this Thread. If it is
then ErrorMgrThread.reun will invoke ErrorMgr.resolveError() which will
cause methods of the ErrorHandlerto be called as appropriate. If no
ErrorHandler is installed then the Error will be rethrown

If no ErrorHandler is installed then the using of an ErrorMgrThread is
completely equivalent to the using of a java.lang.Thread.

classes.name: ErrorMgr
classes.docu:
ErrorMgr provides a unified framework for Error handling. Although ErrorMgr
can handle any type Error, the motivation for ErrorMgr is the handling
of OutOfMemoryErrors. When an OutOfMemoryError occurs in one thread, it is
not unusual for another Thread to also generate an OutOfMemoryError. The
recovery from an OOME can be done in a more orderly manner if there are
not multiple Threads trying to recover concurrently. ErrorMgr provides
a mechanism that will allow one Thread to complete its recovery mechanism
before other Threads are allowed to begin.

ErrorMgr also provides a mechanism for handling Errors that occur on the
DispatchThread during calls to invokeLater() and invokeAndWait().

The contract with the user of ErrorMgr is as follows

1) every Thread should have an ErrorHandler. A newly created Thread will
inherit an ErrorHandler from its parent Thread. If the parent's ErrorHandler
is not appropriate for the new Thread, it should call the static method
ErrorMgr.setErrorHandler to install an ErrorHandler. If a Thread does not
have an ErrorHandler then calls to resolveError() are no-op calls

2) any code that creates a new Thread or a new TimerTask should create a
new ErrorMgrThread or a new ErrorMgrTimerTask instead. Any Object that
extends -Thread- or extends -TimerTask- should extend ErrorMgrThread or
ErrorMgrTimerTask instead.

3) all calls to SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait() should be replaced with calls
to ErrorMgr.invokeAndWait(). All calls to SwingUtilities.invokeLater()
should be replaced by calls to ErrorMgr.invokeLater()

In return ErrorMgr makes the following guarantees

1) The ErrorHandler that has been set for the thread will be called when
the Thread calls ErrorMgr.resolveError(). Note that resolveError may be
called on a thread other than the thread on which the ErrorHandler is
running. For example threads from the ThreadPool will typically be
configured to use the ErrorHandler of the thread for which they are
doing work.

2) multiple ErrorHandlers will not be run concurrently.

3) ErrorMgr will -attempt- to make some heap available for the use of
the ErrorHandler before it calls resolveError(). The ErrorHandler should
use as little heap as possible and should release any heap that is used.
ErrorMgr can not guarantee that it will make any heap available, but will
attempt to free a previously allocated block of size HEAP_RESERVE_SIZE_KB

methods.name: invokeLater
methods.docu:
invokeLater() will place a runnable on the dispatch thread but will
also arrange to handle any errors (e.g. OutOfMemoryError) that occur
during the run of the runnable

if no EventHandler is installed on the calling Thread then a
call to ErrorMgr.invokeLater() is equivalent to a call to
SwingUtilities.invokeLater

**Parameters:**

- `p_runnable` the Runnable that is to be run on the dispatch thread

methods.name: invokeAndWait
methods.docu:
invokeAndWait() will place a runnable on the dispatch thread but will
also arrange to handle any errors (e.g. OutOfMemoryError) that occur
during the run of the runnable

if no ErrorHandler is installed on the calling Thread then
a call to ErrorMgr.invokeAndWait() is equivalent to a call to
SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait();

**Parameters:**

- `p_source` the Object that has invoked the call.
- `p_runnable` the Runnable that is to be run on the dispatch thread

methods.name: invokeAndWait
methods.docu:
this version of invokeAndWait should be called by code that may
(or may not) be executed on the dispatchThread. It allows the caller
to supply the ErrorHandler at the time of the call. Since the
method invokeAndWait(Object, Runnable) assumes that the calling thread
has an ErrorHandler, it will not work correctly if called from the
dispatch thread (which has no handler)

classes.name: ErrorMgrTimerTask2
classes.docu:
This TimerTask allows the real task to extend the java.util.TimerTask.
Subclasses should implement the abstract method runImpl(). This class
implements run() as a final method in terms of runImpl().

Note: This class maintains a strong reference to the ErrorHandler
passed in until cancel() is called on this TimerTask.
